247	which bounds what a camera app or browser history kept of the URL.
248	
249	## The UI
250	
251	**The host** (`src/ui/remote.rs`): `pairing` (`:141`) builds the payload
252	with `invite_url` instead of the JSON (`:160-166`). The text beside the
253	QR changes from "Scan, or type the key and the code" to "Scan with a
254	phone's camera, or type the key and the code in the headset", followed by
255	the warning sentence from decision 1. The paired-devices dialog (`:230`)
256	gains one line under its heading with that sentence. A browser appears in
257	the list by its name, with scope combo and Revoke as every device does.
258	
259	**The page** (`web/index.html`, `web/app.css`, `web/app.js`; no framework,
260	no build step, no dependency; light and dark by `prefers-color-scheme`;
261	one column at phone width):
262	
263	- *Header*: the host name, its short key, the device's scope
264	  (`read`/`control`) from `/me`, and a connection dot.
265	- *List*: sessions grouped by project, the waiting ones first and marked,
266	  each with its name, `kind`, `liveness` and `card` label, and for a
267	  waiting session `waiting_reason`.
268	- *Session view*: the last response (`last-response`, `text`, with
269	  `truncated` said) for a Claude Code session, or the screen
270	  (`screen?lines=200`, monospace) for anything else, refreshed on
271	  `changed`. If `trust_question` is true, a "Folder trust question" line
272	  and a Trust button for a `control` device.
273	- *Reply box*: shown for a `control` device only. It posts
274	  `sessions/{id}/send` with `{op, text}`, with `op` a UUID per click
275	  (`crypto.randomUUID`, falling back to `getRandomValues`, since a
276	  click-through origin may not be a secure context). A timeout is followed
277	  by `GET ops/{op}`, never a blind resend (§4.5).
278	- *States said plainly*: unpaired, pairing closed, wrong key, "identity
279	  changed, pair again", "revoked", host unreachable (retrying), and the
280	  429 and 503 refusals.
281	
282	## The tests
283	
284	The tests are named in the order of the pieces above. The existing
285	`the_allowlist_refuses_everything_else_with_no_side_effect`
286	(`tests/remote.rs:682`) must keep passing.
287	
288	`tests/remote.rs`: `http()` (`:245`) drops response headers, so a second
289	helper returns `(status, headers, body)` and `http` wraps it. Then:
290	
291	- **Static paths.** Each of the three answers 200 with its `Content-Type`
292	  and the full header set, with no `Set-Cookie`. The CSP contains no
293	  `unsafe-inline`, no `http:` or `https:` source and no `*`. A
294	  `POST` to `/` is 405.
295	- **Not in the set.** `/app.js.map`, `/web/`, `/index.html`, `//`,
296	  `/../Cargo.toml` and `/app.js/` are 404, and each is refused to an
297	  unpaired caller (no file read).
298	- **The page is self-consistent.** Every `src` and `href` in the embedded
299	  HTML is a path the host serves. Every `"/api/v1/…"` literal in `app.js`
300	  matches a row of the §4.3 allowlist (the test keeps a table), so a typo
301	  is caught. `app.js` contains no `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`,
302	  `document.write`, `eval` or `new Function`.
303	- **Rate.** The 61st page request in a minute is 429, in the shape of
304	  `pair_is_rate_limited_per_listener` (`:1406`).
305	- **Pairing end to end, as the CLI does it.** Build the URL with
306	  `invite_url`, parse it back, compare `key` with `/info`, `POST /pair`
307	  with `"session":"cookie"`. Assert the `Set-Cookie` attributes
308	  (`__Host-`, `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, no
309	  `Domain`) and no `token` in the body. Then `GET /me` and a read with the
310	  cookie and no bearer succeed. A bearer-only pairing and read behave as
311	  before.
312	- **Origin.** A cookie `POST …/send` with a foreign or missing `Origin` is
313	  403 `origin` and sends nothing to the pane; with the right one it is
314	  typed once per op. The upgrade with a foreign `Origin` is refused; with
315	  the right one it gets `hello`. A bearer request with no `Origin` is
316	  unaffected.
317	- **Revoke** (extend `:658`): after `RevokeDevice`, the cookie's `GET /me`
318	  is 401 `unauthorized`, and a subscribed cookie device's socket closes.
319	  A scope change shows in `/me` on the next call.
320	- **Fixtures** (`write_fixtures`, `:1587`): none added. `/me` is read only
321	  by the page, and no Swift type decodes it.
322

# Plan: a web control surface on the remote port (issue #230)

Line references are to the worktree at `7fe8949` (branch
`dispatch/230-a-web-control-surface-the-remote-port-se`, clean).

## Where this departs from the issue

- **"The key in the URL lets a genuine page refuse to send the code to a
  host whose `/info` key differs."** The code does not bear out the
  strength of that. `/info` returns `spki_sha256` as a JSON string
  (`remote_info`, `src/app.rs:3568`) over the same TLS connection the
  page was loaded on, and a page script cannot see the connection's
  actual public key. A host that terminates TLS can serve a page and an
  `/info` that agree with each other. The comparison catches a stale or
  mistyped QR that points at a different Switchboard, and nothing else.
  The plan keeps the comparison, says what it covers in the spec and in
  the dialog, and makes the owner's click on the certificate warning,
  checked against the key the Mac shows, the trust step (decision 1).
- **"The one-line excerpt the card shows."** The excerpt is not on the
  wire. It is built in the UI from the parsed conversation
  (`agent_excerpt`, `src/ui/cards.rs:558`, called at `:178`) or from a
  pane caption. `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:646` and the fields in
  `client/Fixtures/session.json`) carries `card`, the state label
  (`"starting"`, `"at a prompt (…)"`, `"exited (0)"`), plus
  `waiting_reason` and `notes`. Putting an excerpt in a listing means a
  transcript parse per session, which §4.1 keeps off the frame. The
  first cut shows the `card` label, and `waiting_reason` for a waiting
  session. The last response arrives on opening the session. An excerpt
  is a later, separate read-model item.
- **"A device's scope on the page."** The scope is only in the `/pair`
  reply, and a dialog change takes effect on the next request. After a
  reload the page cannot know it, and it cannot read its cookie. The
  plan adds `GET /api/v1/me`. The issue lists no endpoint, but the
  device's scope, "revoked" and "still paired" all need one.
- **"Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused."** True today
  (`strip_prefix("/api/v1/")`, `src/app.rs:3023`, and the 404 above it).
  The plan serves exactly three fixed paths outside it, before the
  frame is involved. It does not widen the prefix match.
- **"The `/pair` reply"** is `{token, scope, server_id, device_id}`
  (`src/app.rs:3656`). Decision 2 needs the token kept from script, so a
  browser asks for a cookie and its reply has no `token`. The native
  clients' request and reply are unchanged, so `pair.json` still decodes.

## The record

No change to any record. A browser is a `PairedDevice` (`src/ports/remote.rs:96`:
id, name, scope, `token_sha256`, created, `last_seen`) in `devices.json`,
saved through `RemoteFiles::save_devices` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:83`)
and found by `device_by_token` (`src/core/remote.rs:145`). Its name is
`device_name` from the page ("Safari on iPhone", from `navigator.userAgent`),
which `remote_pair` already takes (`src/app.rs:3650`) and defaults to
"Device". No `kind` field is added, so none of these versions moves:
`SCHEMA_VERSION` (16, `src/core/model.rs:12`), `VIEWS_SCHEMA_VERSION`
(7, `src/core/model.rs:612`) and `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` (1,
`src/ports/remote.rs:17`). `devices.json` has no version of its own, only
the array. Should an implementer find a device kind necessary after all,
the bump is the value in `model.rs` or `ports/remote.rs` at that time plus
one, with a step in `adapters::store::migrate`. Another ticket may have
taken the next number first.

**Rehydration.** The host side is nothing new. The page keeps no state on
the host, `devices.json` survives a restart, and the same token hash is
accepted. `epoch` changes on restart and the page refetches (§4.4). The
device side is new, and has two parts:

1. The token, in an `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` cookie that
   script never reads (decision 2).
2. A non-secret `localStorage` entry `{server_id, spki_sha256, name}`
   written at pairing, in a `try`. Without it the page cannot tell
   "never paired" from "revoked" or "identity changed", because it
   cannot read the cookie. A reload does this:
   - read the entry;
   - `GET /info`, and compare `server_id` and `spki_sha256`: a mismatch
     shows "identity changed, pair again" and sends nothing;
   - `GET /me`: 401 with an entry shows "revoked" and clears the entry,
     401 without one shows the unpaired screen.

   With `localStorage` unavailable the page still works for the session
   and shows the unpaired screen after a reload that finds no cookie.

The origin is `https://<ip>:<port>`, so cookie and entry belong to that
address. A Mac whose address changes is a new origin to the browser and
needs pairing again. The spec says so as a known gap, because a phone has
no Bonjour to follow the host.

## The signals

None new. The page is a fourth speaker of the existing protocol (§4.4):
it opens `wss://<host>/api/v1/events`, waits for `hello`, snapshots
`projects`, `projects/{id}/sessions` and `waiting`, applies buffered
events by revision, and refetches on `changed {session | sessions |
waiting | projects}`. A session that starts waiting changes the `waiting`
collection, so it moves to the top without a reload. For the open session
it sends `watch {conversation | screen}` when the view opens and
`unwatch` on leaving, and refetches on `changed`. On `resync_required` or
a new `epoch` it reloads everything, and it reconnects with back-off.
Redaction (§4.3) is applied before every cut on the host and is unchanged.
The page renders every host-supplied string with `textContent`, never
`innerHTML`, so a transcript cannot inject markup even if the CSP were
relaxed. The spec states that rule, and a test enforces it.

## The actions and effects

No `AppAction`, no `Effect`, no core state: serving a page and
authenticating a cookie are the port's job (`src/adapters/remote.rs`,
`serve_remote`), as `/info` is. Pairing, revoking and scope changes
already go through `Paired`, `RevokeDevice` and `SetDeviceScope`.

**Decision 1: the certificate.** Click-through, not a downloadable
certificate. A downloaded certificate must be installed and then trusted
in full on the device (on iOS a profile, then Certificate Trust Settings).
That flow is heavy and easy to get wrong. It also trusts the certificate
for every name the device reaches, a wider grant than a per-address
exception. The click-through grants one browser an exception for one
address, which is all this surface needs. What it buys is encryption on
the wire and a browser that remembers the exception. What it does not buy
is any proof of whose certificate it is: on a hostile network an impostor
can present its own, and the owner's click is what lets it. So the step
the owner performs is a comparison. The pairing window already shows
`Key xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx` (`short_hash`, `src/ui/remote.rs:303`). The page
shows the same sixteen digits in its header from `/info`, before and after
pairing. The window's text and the paired-devices dialog say it in one
sentence: "A browser trusts this Mac by your click on its certificate
warning, on a network you trust. Check the key on the page against this
one." The certificate stays as `make_identity` makes it
(`src/adapters/remote.rs:95`, no SubjectAltName). The spike records
whether Safari and Chrome offer "proceed" for it. If either does not, the
fix is an IP SAN added when the certificate is made at serve time. The
pin is the key, so reissuing the certificate invalidates no pairing.
`a_change_of_address_rebinds_the_port` (`tests/remote.rs:1494`) is where
that would be tested.

§5's rule is kept and amended: **before pairing, no bind serves anything
but `/info`, `/pair` and the page's own three files.** Every other path is
refused, loopback or not.

**Decision 2: the token reaches the socket as a cookie.**
`POST /api/v1/pair` takes an extra body field `"session": "cookie"`. The
reply then omits `token` and sets
`Set-Cookie: __Host-sb=<token>; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=34560000`
(400 days, the cap browsers apply; the token does not expire and
revocation is the host's). A script never holds the token, `fetch` and
`new WebSocket` both carry the cookie, and the token is in no URL and no
`Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`. `localStorage` is readable by any script on the
origin and a cookie is not, which settles where the token lives. Native
clients send no `session` field and are unchanged.

`authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127`) takes the token from `Authorization:
Bearer` and, absent that, from the cookie. Cookies are not isolated by
port, so another service on the same IP shares the jar, and the upgrade
request carries the cookie: both are request-forgery surfaces. So a
cookie-authenticated request that is not a `GET`, and every WebSocket
upgrade, must carry `Origin: https://<Host header>`. Otherwise it is
refused 403 `origin` before any command is translated. A bearer request
is never subject to this. Revocation needs no new path. The record is
gone, the cookie's hash is unknown, the next request is 401
`unauthorized`, and the socket closes as it does today.

*If the spike shows a browser refuses to store the `Secure` cookie from a
click-through origin, stop and take that to the owner before building on
it.* The fallback is a `localStorage` token and a single-use ticket for
the socket. That changes the threat model (decision 2 above), so it is not
built speculatively.

**Port changes** (`src/adapters/remote.rs`, `src/app.rs`):

- `RemoteRequest` (`:360`) gains `cookie`, `origin`, `host`
  (`Option<String>`), filled in `read_request` (`:444`) beside `bearer`
  (`:487`). The cookie header is parsed for `__Host-sb` only and dropped
  otherwise; none of the three is logged. `RemoteReply` (`:389`) gains
  `headers: Vec<(String, String)>`, which `respond` (`:530`) writes after
  `Content-Type`. That means adding `headers: Vec::new()` to the 30
  literals (28 in `src/app.rs`, 2 in the adapter), a mechanical edit.
- **Static paths are answered on the connection thread**, in `connection`
  (`:770`) before the request is handed to the frame, from a fixed `match`
  in a new `src/adapters/web.rs` (`pub fn asset(method, path) -> Asset`).
  The path is matched exactly and never joined to anything. They cost the
  frame nothing and do not use the 64-deep inbox. The set, `GET` only
  (anything else on these paths is 405 with `Allow: GET`; the query is
  ignored and never read):

  | Path | `Content-Type` |
  |---|---|
  | `/` | `text/html; charset=utf-8` |
  | `/app.css` | `text/css; charset=utf-8` |
  | `/app.js` | `text/javascript; charset=utf-8` |

  Anything else not under `/api/v1/` stays 404 `not_found` from
  `serve_remote`. Every static reply carries:
  - `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`.
    There is no `unsafe-inline` and no host. The HTML has no inline script
    or style, and carries `<link rel="icon" href="data:,">` so no favicon
    is requested. If the spike shows Safari does not match `'self'` to
    `wss:`, the explicit `wss://<Host>` source is added at serve time.
  - `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
  - `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`. **This is load-bearing:** the page's
    own URL holds the code, and without it the browser sends that URL as
    `Referer` with the request for `/app.js`.
  - `Cache-Control: no-store`, so nothing is cached across versions and no
    version is put in a URL.
  - `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`.
  - Never a `Set-Cookie`.
- **Pools and rate** (`:567-587`, `:631`). A static reply is
  `authenticated: false`, so a browser's connections sit in the pool of 4
  until its first authenticated call (the `events` upgrade or a read) moves
  them to the paired pool (`:835`). A browser may open up to six
  connections for a page. Past four, an accept is closed at once and the
  browser retries. The page is three files so keep-alive covers it with
  one or two. The pools are not changed: the spike counts the connections
  of a real page load, and only a measured failure changes the pool
  accounting. The only addition is `PAGE_PER_MINUTE = 60` (a new
  `RateWindow` in `Limits`, `:631`), shared by the three paths and
  answered 429 on the connection thread as `/info` is. A load is three
  requests, so twenty loads a minute.
- **`GET /api/v1/me`** (`serve_remote`, after `authenticate`): `{device_id,
  name, scope}`, any paired device. The cheapest "am I still paired" probe
  and the one the revoke test polls. It goes in the §4.3 table.
- **Unpaired with no code and no cookie**, the page shows the host name
  and key (`/info`), "Not paired", and "Open Remote devices on the Mac,
  allow pairing, and scan its QR code", with `pairing_open` from `/info`.
  With a code and pairing closed (403 `pairing_closed`) it says so. On
  `wrong_key` it says "this is not the host whose code was scanned". On
  `wrong_code` it says the code was wrong or used.

**Decision 3: one URL.** The pairing window's payload becomes
`https://<ip>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>` (the
address is IPv4, from `local_address`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:962`; the
alphabet needs no escaping). A pure
`core::remote::invite_url(address, server_id, spki, code)` builds it, so a
core test pins the shape. The QR, the text beside it and "Copy invite"
carry the URL. The JSON is dropped from the host. Nothing needs it once
the native text paths accept the URL, so there is one invite, not two. The
Swift side keeps decoding the JSON, for old pasted invites and the
fixture tests. `PairingInvite.parse` (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:114`)
reads JSON when the text starts with `{`, else a URL, taking `addresses`
from its host and port, `key` as `spkiSha256`, `id` as `serverID`. It is
the single entry for the CLI (`main.swift:107`) and for the headset's paste
(`BrowserView.swift:106`, `:883`), so neither changes beyond `main.swift`'s
usage text (`:10`). `switchboard-remote pair` keeps both forms: one
argument (URL or JSON) or three.

**The code in a GET.** The browser requests `/?code=…`. `read_request`
already parses a query (`:497`), the static arm never reads it, and
`refuse` logs method and path only. `app.js` begins with
`history.replaceState(null, "", "/")` after copying the three values into
locals, before any request. The code is single-use and lives five minutes,
which bounds what a camera app or browser history kept of the URL.

## The UI

**The host** (`src/ui/remote.rs`): `pairing` (`:141`) builds the payload
with `invite_url` instead of the JSON (`:160-166`). The text beside the
QR changes from "Scan, or type the key and the code" to "Scan with a
phone's camera, or type the key and the code in the headset", followed by
the warning sentence from decision 1. The paired-devices dialog (`:230`)
gains one line under its heading with that sentence. A browser appears in
the list by its name, with scope combo and Revoke as every device does.

**The page** (`web/index.html`, `web/app.css`, `web/app.js`; no framework,
no build step, no dependency; light and dark by `prefers-color-scheme`;
one column at phone width):

- *Header*: the host name, its short key, the device's scope
  (`read`/`control`) from `/me`, and a connection dot.
- *List*: sessions grouped by project, the waiting ones first and marked,
  each with its name, `kind`, `liveness` and `card` label, and for a
  waiting session `waiting_reason`.
- *Session view*: the last response (`last-response`, `text`, with
  `truncated` said) for a Claude Code session, or the screen
  (`screen?lines=200`, monospace) for anything else, refreshed on
  `changed`. If `trust_question` is true, a "Folder trust question" line
  and a Trust button for a `control` device.
- *Reply box*: shown for a `control` device only. It posts
  `sessions/{id}/send` with `{op, text}`, with `op` a UUID per click
  (`crypto.randomUUID`, falling back to `getRandomValues`, since a
  click-through origin may not be a secure context). A timeout is followed
  by `GET ops/{op}`, never a blind resend (§4.5).
- *States said plainly*: unpaired, pairing closed, wrong key, "identity
  changed, pair again", "revoked", host unreachable (retrying), and the
  429 and 503 refusals.

## The tests

The tests are named in the order of the pieces above. The existing
`the_allowlist_refuses_everything_else_with_no_side_effect`
(`tests/remote.rs:682`) must keep passing.

`tests/remote.rs`: `http()` (`:245`) drops response headers, so a second
helper returns `(status, headers, body)` and `http` wraps it. Then:

- **Static paths.** Each of the three answers 200 with its `Content-Type`
  and the full header set, with no `Set-Cookie`. The CSP contains no
  `unsafe-inline`, no `http:` or `https:` source and no `*`. A
  `POST` to `/` is 405.
- **Not in the set.** `/app.js.map`, `/web/`, `/index.html`, `//`,
  `/../Cargo.toml` and `/app.js/` are 404, and each is refused to an
  unpaired caller (no file read).
- **The page is self-consistent.** Every `src` and `href` in the embedded
  HTML is a path the host serves. Every `"/api/v1/…"` literal in `app.js`
  matches a row of the §4.3 allowlist (the test keeps a table), so a typo
  is caught. `app.js` contains no `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`,
  `document.write`, `eval` or `new Function`.
- **Rate.** The 61st page request in a minute is 429, in the shape of
  `pair_is_rate_limited_per_listener` (`:1406`).
- **Pairing end to end, as the CLI does it.** Build the URL with
  `invite_url`, parse it back, compare `key` with `/info`, `POST /pair`
  with `"session":"cookie"`. Assert the `Set-Cookie` attributes
  (`__Host-`, `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, no
  `Domain`) and no `token` in the body. Then `GET /me` and a read with the
  cookie and no bearer succeed. A bearer-only pairing and read behave as
  before.
- **Origin.** A cookie `POST …/send` with a foreign or missing `Origin` is
  403 `origin` and sends nothing to the pane; with the right one it is
  typed once per op. The upgrade with a foreign `Origin` is refused; with
  the right one it gets `hello`. A bearer request with no `Origin` is
  unaffected.
- **Revoke** (extend `:658`): after `RevokeDevice`, the cookie's `GET /me`
  is 401 `unauthorized`, and a subscribed cookie device's socket closes.
  A scope change shows in `/me` on the next call.
- **Fixtures** (`write_fixtures`, `:1587`): none added. `/me` is read only
  by the page, and no Swift type decodes it.

`tests/ui.rs`: extend `remote_devices_dialog_opens_pairing_and_revokes_a_device`
(`:7424`). Its clipboard assertions (`:7484-7492`) parse the invite as JSON
today. They become: the text starts with `https://`, and its `code`, `key`
and `id` query values are the window's code, the identity's `spki_sha256`
and its `server_id`. The dialog text shows the certificate sentence.

`src/core/tests.rs`: `invite_url` is exact for a known input.

Swift (`client/Tests/SwitchboardClientCoreTests/PairingTests.swift`):
`parse` accepts the URL form and the old JSON, and refuses a URL with no
`code`. Run with `swift test` in `client/`, which CI does not.

No JS test runner exists and the issue forbids a build step, so the page's
behavior is covered by the acceptance below, done by hand on a phone.

**Spike first** (CLAUDE.md): `spikes/23-web-surface/README.md` with
measured results, written before the page is relied on. It answers on
Safari on an iPhone and Chrome on a Mac:
- does a click-through certificate (as `make_identity` makes it) get a
  "proceed" option, and is a `__Host-` `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`
  cookie stored from it, sent on `fetch` and on `wss://`;
- does `connect-src 'self'` allow the same-origin `wss://`;
- how many connections a page load opens against the pool of 4;
- does the camera open the `https://ip:port/?…` URL, and does `replaceState`
  keep the code out of the history.

The spike needs a phone; an implementer without one records which rows
are unmeasured, and the owner's acceptance run closes them.

**Acceptance** (the issue's, by hand): open the pairing window, scan with a
phone, accept the warning, see the sessions; start a session waiting and
watch it move to the top; send a reply and see it arrive; revoke the phone
in the dialog and the page says "revoked" on its next request.

## Docs, in the same commit

- `docs/remote-client.md`:
  - §4.1: the page rate and the pool note;

1	1. **Decision 1's trust step proves nothing, and contradicts the plan's own first departure.** The plan has the owner "check the key on the page against" the key in the pairing window. But the page's key comes from `/info`, which is served by whatever host terminates TLS. An impostor that the owner clicks through can relay the real host's `/info` and show the genuine 16 digits. The plan concedes this in its first bullet ("a host that terminates TLS can serve a page and an `/info` that agree"), then relies on the same comparison in Decision 1 and in the user-facing sentence ("Check the key on the page against this one"). A browser's certificate viewer shows the certificate fingerprint, not the SPKI hash, so the owner cannot compare against it either. docs/remote-client.md §5 and design.md's "Trust boundary" are binding: "Pairing verifies the key before the code is sent." This design sends the code (in the GET URL, then in `/pair`) to an unverified peer, and the token comes back to that peer as a `Set-Cookie`. The plan needs one of these:
2	   - a real owner-checkable binding, such as the SPKI hash shown in a form the browser exposes, or an IP SAN plus a fingerprint the owner can read in the certificate dialog;
3	   - an explicit amendment to the "key verified before the code is sent" rule, written into design.md and §5 as a deliberate weakening, with the owner's sign-off;
4	   - removing the "check the key on the page" instruction, since it gives false assurance.
5	
6	2. **Dropping the JSON invite breaks the additive-contract rule and shipped clients.** CLAUDE.md says to extend the contract additively and never remove. The plan replaces the QR and "Copy invite" payload (`src/ui/remote.rs:160-166`) with a URL and drops the JSON "from the host". Already-installed native clients decode only the JSON. Swift's `parse` already falls back to a URL, but only in the plan's new version. The JSON also carries `addresses`, which can hold several entries, while the URL carries one. Keep the JSON available, for example behind a separate "Copy invite for headset" or as a field of the URL, or state the break and justify it. As written, "one invite, not two" is a removal.
7	
8	3. **Reachability is not addressed.** `bind_remote` (`src/app.rs:2924`) binds loopback until the owner allows the local network. A phone cannot load the page or `/pair` at all until then. The plan says nothing about the pairing window or its QR when the bind is loopback-only. The URL uses `local_address()`, which may not be the bound interface. State what the pairing window shows in that case (a prompt to enable LAN, or the QR suppressed) and test it.
9	
10	4. **The origin rule is incomplete.** The plan checks `Origin` against the `Host` header, and both are attacker-influenced in the DNS-rebinding and shared-cookie scenarios it names. It also exempts every cookie `GET`. `GET …/screen`, `last-response` and `events` are the redacted content. With a shared cookie jar across ports, a hostile page on the same IP can issue credentialed cross-origin `GET`s, and the response is not readable but timing is. Also, `SameSite=Strict` does not cover other ports on the same site. Decide whether cookie `GET`s should require `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` or `Origin` too. Also say what happens when a browser sends no `Origin` on a same-origin `GET`: the plan says "missing" is refused for `POST` only, and the upgrade rule is inconsistent with that for old browsers.
11	
12	5. **Two hosts on one IP share one cookie.** The cookie is `__Host-sb`, `Path=/`, and cookies ignore ports. A second Switchboard instance on another port (the plan itself notes `SWITCHBOARD_REMOTE_PORT`) overwrites the first host's token, and each sees the other's token as unknown. The plan only notes this as a forgery surface. It needs a per-`server_id` cookie name, which `__Host-` allows, or it must state the limitation and the revoke-on-401 behavior it causes. As written, the page would show "revoked" and clear the `localStorage` entry on a mere collision.
13	
14	6. **`/me` is not in the "no new endpoint" accounting.** `GET /api/v1/me` is an additive contract change. It is listed in the commit body, but the plan says "fixtures: none added" because only the page reads it. CLAUDE.md puts the wire in `docs/remote-client.md` §4.3 as the shared contract, and the Swift side has a fixtures test pattern (`write_fixtures`, `tests/remote.rs:1587`). Say whether `/me` needs a fixture so a native client can decode it, or why not.
15	
16	7. **Rate-limit accounting is under-specified.** `Limits::limited` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:630`) matches an exact path against `PAIR_PATH` and `INFO_PATH`. `PAGE_PER_MINUTE` needs three paths sharing one window, and the plan does not say how `limited` is changed. With a single shared window, a normal reload (3 requests) plus a reconnect storm could lock out the owner's own page. The 429 for a static path also needs the same CSP and headers or none, and the plan is silent on that. Say which.

18	8. **The page's JS has no automated test, yet the plan makes security claims about it.** The plan relies on "`textContent` never `innerHTML`" and the Origin and cookie behaviors working in a browser, and covers them by grep-style tests and a manual acceptance run on a phone. The plan commits to a "Spike first" that needs a phone. If the spike's Safari row fails (no `Secure` cookie from a click-through origin, as the plan itself anticipates), Decision 2 collapses and the plan stops. The order lists the spike as step 1 of a single commit, so the whole design is unresolved at plan time. Mark Decision 2 as conditional in the plan's contract and commit message, or split the spike into its own commit that gates the rest, consistent with CLAUDE.md ("add a new spike directory for any new risky mechanism before building on it").

13	  actual public key. A host that terminates TLS can serve a page and an
14	  `/info` that agree with each other. The comparison catches a stale or
15	  mistyped QR that points at a different Switchboard, and nothing else.

18	  checked against the key the Mac shows, the trust step (decision 1).

57	the bump is the value in `model.rs` or `ports/remote.rs` at that time plus
58	one, with a step in `adapters::store::migrate`. Another ticket may have
59	taken the next number first.
60	
61	**Rehydration.** The host side is nothing new. The page keeps no state on
62	the host, `devices.json` survives a restart, and the same token hash is
63	accepted. `epoch` changes on restart and the page refetches (§4.4). The
64	device side is new, and has two parts:
65	
66	1. The token, in an `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` cookie that
67	   script never reads (decision 2).
68	2. A non-secret `localStorage` entry `{server_id, spki_sha256, name}`
69	   written at pairing, in a `try`. Without it the page cannot tell
70	   "never paired" from "revoked" or "identity changed", because it
71	   cannot read the cookie. A reload does this:
72	   - read the entry;
73	   - `GET /info`, and compare `server_id` and `spki_sha256`: a mismatch
74	     shows "identity changed, pair again" and sends nothing;
75	   - `GET /me`: 401 with an entry shows "revoked" and clears the entry,
76	     401 without one shows the unpaired screen.
77	
78	   With `localStorage` unavailable the page still works for the session
79	   and shows the unpaired screen after a reload that finds no cookie.
80	
81	The origin is `https://<ip>:<port>`, so cookie and entry belong to that
82	address. A Mac whose address changes is a new origin to the browser and
83	needs pairing again. The spec says so as a known gap, because a phone has
84	no Bonjour to follow the host.

87	
88	None new. The page is a fourth speaker of the existing protocol (§4.4):
89	it opens `wss://<host>/api/v1/events`, waits for `hello`, snapshots
90	`projects`, `projects/{id}/sessions` and `waiting`, applies buffered
91	events by revision, and refetches on `changed {session | sessions |
92	waiting | projects}`. A session that starts waiting changes the `waiting`
93	collection, so it moves to the top without a reload. For the open session
94	it sends `watch {conversation | screen}` when the view opens and
95	`unwatch` on leaving, and refetches on `changed`. On `resync_required` or
96	a new `epoch` it reloads everything, and it reconnects with back-off.
97	Redaction (§4.3) is applied before every cut on the host and is unchanged.
98	The page renders every host-supplied string with `textContent`, never
99	`innerHTML`, so a transcript cannot inject markup even if the CSP were
100	relaxed. The spec states that rule, and a test enforces it.
101	
102	## The actions and effects
103	
104	No `AppAction`, no `Effect`, no core state: serving a page and
105	authenticating a cookie are the port's job (`src/adapters/remote.rs`,
106	`serve_remote`), as `/info` is. Pairing, revoking and scope changes
107	already go through `Paired`, `RevokeDevice` and `SetDeviceScope`.
108	
109	**Decision 1: the certificate.** Click-through, not a downloadable
110	certificate. A downloaded certificate must be installed and then trusted
111	in full on the device (on iOS a profile, then Certificate Trust Settings).
112	That flow is heavy and easy to get wrong. It also trusts the certificate
113	for every name the device reaches, a wider grant than a per-address
114	exception. The click-through grants one browser an exception for one
115	address, which is all this surface needs. What it buys is encryption on
116	the wire and a browser that remembers the exception. What it does not buy
117	is any proof of whose certificate it is: on a hostile network an impostor
118	can present its own, and the owner's click is what lets it. So the step
119	the owner performs is a comparison. The pairing window already shows
120	`Key xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx` (`short_hash`, `src/ui/remote.rs:303`). The page
121	shows the same sixteen digits in its header from `/info`, before and after
122	pairing. The window's text and the paired-devices dialog say it in one
123	sentence: "A browser trusts this Mac by your click on its certificate
124	warning, on a network you trust. Check the key on the page against this
125	one." The certificate stays as `make_identity` makes it
126	(`src/adapters/remote.rs:95`, no SubjectAltName). The spike records

129	pin is the key, so reissuing the certificate invalidates no pairing.
130	`a_change_of_address_rebinds_the_port` (`tests/remote.rs:1494`) is where

139	reply then omits `token` and sets
140	`Set-Cookie: __Host-sb=<token>; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=34560000`

142	revocation is the host's). A script never holds the token, `fetch` and

146	clients send no `session` field and are unchanged.
147	
148	`authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127`) takes the token from `Authorization:

152	cookie-authenticated request that is not a `GET`, and every WebSocket
153	upgrade, must carry `Origin: https://<Host header>`. Otherwise it is

155	is never subject to this. Revocation needs no new path. The record is
156	gone, the cookie's hash is unknown, the next request is 401

158

174	- **Static paths are answered on the connection thread**, in `connection`
175	  (`:770`) before the request is handed to the frame, from a fixed `match`
176	  in a new `src/adapters/web.rs` (`pub fn asset(method, path) -> Asset`).
177	  The path is matched exactly and never joined to anything. They cost the
178	  frame nothing and do not use the 64-deep inbox. The set, `GET` only
179	  (anything else on these paths is 405 with `Allow: GET`; the query is
180	  ignored and never read):
181	
182	  | Path | `Content-Type` |
183	  |---|---|
184	  | `/` | `text/html; charset=utf-8` |
185	  | `/app.css` | `text/css; charset=utf-8` |
186	  | `/app.js` | `text/javascript; charset=utf-8` |
187	
188	  Anything else not under `/api/v1/` stays 404 `not_found` from
189	  `serve_remote`. Every static reply carries:
190	  - `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`.

201	  - `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`.
202	  - Never a `Set-Cookie`.
203	- **Pools and rate** (`:567-587`, `:631`). A static reply is
204	  `authenticated: false`, so a browser's connections sit in the pool of 4
205	  until its first authenticated call (the `events` upgrade or a read) moves
206	  them to the paired pool (`:835`). A browser may open up to six
207	  connections for a page. Past four, an accept is closed at once and the
208	  browser retries. The page is three files so keep-alive covers it with
209	  one or two. The pools are not changed: the spike counts the connections
210	  of a real page load, and only a measured failure changes the pool
211	  accounting. The only addition is `PAGE_PER_MINUTE = 60` (a new
212	  `RateWindow` in `Limits`, `:631`), shared by the three paths and
213	  answered 429 on the connection thread as `/info` is. A load is three
214	  requests, so twenty loads a minute.
215	- **`GET /api/v1/me`** (`serve_remote`, after `authenticate`): `{device_id,
216	  name, scope}`, any paired device. The cheapest "am I still paired" probe
217	  and the one the revoke test polls. It goes in the §4.3 table.
218	- **Unpaired with no code and no cookie**, the page shows the host name
219	  and key (`/info`), "Not paired", and "Open Remote devices on the Mac,
220	  allow pairing, and scan its QR code", with `pairing_open` from `/info`.
221	  With a code and pairing closed (403 `pairing_closed`) it says so. On
222	  `wrong_key` it says "this is not the host whose code was scanned". On
223	  `wrong_code` it says the code was wrong or used.
224	
225	**Decision 3: one URL.** The pairing window's payload becomes
226	`https://<ip>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>` (the
227	address is IPv4, from `local_address`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:962`; the
228	alphabet needs no escaping). A pure
229	`core::remote::invite_url(address, server_id, spki, code)` builds it, so a
230	core test pins the shape. The QR, the text beside it and "Copy invite"
231	carry the URL. The JSON is dropped from the host. Nothing needs it once
232	the native text paths accept the URL, so there is one invite, not two. The
233	Swift side keeps decoding the JSON, for old pasted invites and the
234	fixture tests. `PairingInvite.parse` (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:114`)
235	reads JSON when the text starts with `{`, else a URL, taking `addresses`
236	from its host and port, `key` as `spkiSha256`, `id` as `serverID`. It is
237	the single entry for the CLI (`main.swift:107`) and for the headset's paste
238	(`BrowserView.swift:106`, `:883`), so neither changes beyond `main.swift`'s
239	usage text (`:10`). `switchboard-remote pair` keeps both forms: one
240	argument (URL or JSON) or three.
241	
242	**The code in a GET.** The browser requests `/?code=…`. `read_request`
243	already parses a query (`:497`), the static arm never reads it, and
244	`refuse` logs method and path only. `app.js` begins with
245	`history.replaceState(null, "", "/")` after copying the three values into
246	locals, before any request. The code is single-use and lives five minutes,
247	which bounds what a camera app or browser history kept of the URL.
248	
249	## The UI
250	
251	**The host** (`src/ui/remote.rs`): `pairing` (`:141`) builds the payload
252	with `invite_url` instead of the JSON (`:160-166`). The text beside the
253	QR changes from "Scan, or type the key and the code" to "Scan with a
254	phone's camera, or type the key and the code in the headset", followed by
255	the warning sentence from decision 1. The paired-devices dialog (`:230`)
256	gains one line under its heading with that sentence. A browser appears in
257	the list by its name, with scope combo and Revoke as every device does.
258	
259	**The page** (`web/index.html`, `web/app.css`, `web/app.js`; no framework,
260	no build step, no dependency; light and dark by `prefers-color-scheme`;
261	one column at phone width):
262	
263	- *Header*: the host name, its short key, the device's scope
264	  (`read`/`control`) from `/me`, and a connection dot.
265	- *List*: sessions grouped by project, the waiting ones first and marked,
266	  each with its name, `kind`, `liveness` and `card` label, and for a
267	  waiting session `waiting_reason`.
268	- *Session view*: the last response (`last-response`, `text`, with
269	  `truncated` said) for a Claude Code session, or the screen
270	  (`screen?lines=200`, monospace) for anything else, refreshed on
271	  `changed`. If `trust_question` is true, a "Folder trust question" line
272	  and a Trust button for a `control` device.
273	- *Reply box*: shown for a `control` device only. It posts
274	  `sessions/{id}/send` with `{op, text}`, with `op` a UUID per click
275	  (`crypto.randomUUID`, falling back to `getRandomValues`, since a
276	  click-through origin may not be a secure context). A timeout is followed
277	  by `GET ops/{op}`, never a blind resend (§4.5).
278	- *States said plainly*: unpaired, pairing closed, wrong key, "identity
279	  changed, pair again", "revoked", host unreachable (retrying), and the
280	  429 and 503 refusals.
281	
282	## The tests
283	
284	The tests are named in the order of the pieces above. The existing
285	`the_allowlist_refuses_everything_else_with_no_side_effect`
286	(`tests/remote.rs:682`) must keep passing.
287	
288	`tests/remote.rs`: `http()` (`:245`) drops response headers, so a second
289	helper returns `(status, headers, body)` and `http` wraps it. Then:
290	
291	- **Static paths.** Each of the three answers 200 with its `Content-Type`
292	  and the full header set, with no `Set-Cookie`. The CSP contains no
293	  `unsafe-inline`, no `http:` or `https:` source and no `*`. A
294	  `POST` to `/` is 405.
295	- **Not in the set.** `/app.js.map`, `/web/`, `/index.html`, `//`,
296	  `/../Cargo.toml` and `/app.js/` are 404, and each is refused to an
297	  unpaired caller (no file read).
298	- **The page is self-consistent.** Every `src` and `href` in the embedded
299	  HTML is a path the host serves. Every `"/api/v1/…"` literal in `app.js`
300	  matches a row of the §4.3 allowlist (the test keeps a table), so a typo
301	  is caught. `app.js` contains no `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`,
302	  `document.write`, `eval` or `new Function`.
303	- **Rate.** The 61st page request in a minute is 429, in the shape of
304	  `pair_is_rate_limited_per_listener` (`:1406`).
305	- **Pairing end to end, as the CLI does it.** Build the URL with
306	  `invite_url`, parse it back, compare `key` with `/info`, `POST /pair`
307	  with `"session":"cookie"`. Assert the `Set-Cookie` attributes
308	  (`__Host-`, `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, no
309	  `Domain`) and no `token` in the body. Then `GET /me` and a read with the
310	  cookie and no bearer succeed. A bearer-only pairing and read behave as
311	  before.
312	- **Origin.** A cookie `POST …/send` with a foreign or missing `Origin` is
313	  403 `origin` and sends nothing to the pane; with the right one it is
314	  typed once per op. The upgrade with a foreign `Origin` is refused; with
315	  the right one it gets `hello`. A bearer request with no `Origin` is
316	  unaffected.
317	- **Revoke** (extend `:658`): after `RevokeDevice`, the cookie's `GET /me`
318	  is 401 `unauthorized`, and a subscribed cookie device's socket closes.
319	  A scope change shows in `/me` on the next call.
320	- **Fixtures** (`write_fixtures`, `:1587`): none added. `/me` is read only
321	  by the page, and no Swift type decodes it.
322	
323	`tests/ui.rs`: extend `remote_devices_dialog_opens_pairing_and_revokes_a_device`
324	(`:7424`). Its clipboard assertions (`:7484-7492`) parse the invite as JSON
325	today. They become: the text starts with `https://`, and its `code`, `key`
326	and `id` query values are the window's code, the identity's `spki_sha256`
327	and its `server_id`. The dialog text shows the certificate sentence.
328	
329	`src/core/tests.rs`: `invite_url` is exact for a known input.
330	
331	Swift (`client/Tests/SwitchboardClientCoreTests/PairingTests.swift`):
332	`parse` accepts the URL form and the old JSON, and refuses a URL with no
333	`code`. Run with `swift test` in `client/`, which CI does not.
334	
335	No JS test runner exists and the issue forbids a build step, so the page's
336	behavior is covered by the acceptance below, done by hand on a phone.
337	
338	**Spike first** (CLAUDE.md): `spikes/23-web-surface/README.md` with
339	measured results, written before the page is relied on. It answers on
340	Safari on an iPhone and Chrome on a Mac:
341	- does a click-through certificate (as `make_identity` makes it) get a
342	  "proceed" option, and is a `__Host-` `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`
343	  cookie stored from it, sent on `fetch` and on `wss://`;
344	- does `connect-src 'self'` allow the same-origin `wss://`;
345	- how many connections a page load opens against the pool of 4;
346	- does the camera open the `https://ip:port/?…` URL, and does `replaceState`
347	  keep the code out of the history.
348	
349	The spike needs a phone; an implementer without one records which rows
350	are unmeasured, and the owner's acceptance run closes them.
351	
352	**Acceptance** (the issue's, by hand): open the pairing window, scan with a
353	phone, accept the warning, see the sessions; start a session waiting and
354	watch it move to the top; send a reply and see it arrive; revoke the phone
355	in the dialog and the page says "revoked" on its next request.
356

359	- `docs/remote-client.md`:
360	  - §4.1: the page rate and the pool note;
361	  - §4.3: rows for the three static paths and `/me`;
362	  - §5: the pairing QR is a URL, the browser trust step and what it does
363	    not prove, the cookie (the "sent only as a bearer header" bullet gains
364	    "or the browser's cookie"), the Origin rule, the amended "nothing but
365	    `/info`, `/pair` and the page" rule, and the per-address known gap;
366	  - §11: the tests above;
367	  - a §0 revision note.
368	- `docs/design.md`, "Remote client (2026-10-12)" (`:3107-3584`): a bullet

373	  `spikes/23-web-surface`; the `adapters/remote.rs` row (`:383`) gains the
374	  cookie, the Origin rule and the static paths; the `ui/remote.rs` (`:423`)
375	  and `tests/remote.rs` (`:437`) rows; the dev-aid paragraph (`:267-279`)
376	  says "Copy invite" puts a URL on the clipboard and that

379	- `CHANGELOG.md`, under Unreleased: "A web page on the remote port: scan
380	  the pairing QR code with a phone to see the sessions, which are waiting,
381	  and send a reply."

406	- `RemoteRequest` gains `cookie`, `origin` and `host` (`Option<String>`);
407	  `RemoteReply` gains `headers: Vec<(String, String)>`.

exception. The click-through grants one browser an exception for one
address, which is all this surface needs. What it buys is encryption on
the wire and a browser that remembers the exception. What it does not buy
is any proof of whose certificate it is: on a hostile network an impostor
can present its own, relay the real host's `/info`, show the genuine key
digits, and the owner's click is what lets it. **So the page's key is not
a check and the plan does not tell the owner to compare it.** The page
still shows the host name and short key from `/info`, labelled "as the
host reports it", only to tell two Switchboards apart and to drive the
"identity changed" state. The browser's own certificate viewer shows the
certificate's fingerprint, not the SPKI hash, and a phone's shows neither
usefully, so no comparison is offered there either.

The amendment, for the owner to sign off (this is the one open decision
the plan cannot make): **a browser pairs without the key having been
verified first. The only trust step is the owner's decision to open the
pairing window and scan its QR on a network they trust, with the code
single-use, five minutes and three wrong tries.** What bounds the damage:
the scope is chosen in the window (`read` by default), the new device
appears in the paired-devices dialog by name the moment it pairs, and
Revoke closes it. The window's text and the dialog say so in one
sentence: "A browser cannot verify this Mac's key. Pair a browser only on
a network you trust; check the device appears below, and revoke it if it
is not yours." §5 and the "Remote client" section of design.md gain that
sentence as a deliberate exception for the web page. If the owner declines
the amendment, the web page is not built, and the plan has no second
design to offer: a downloaded, trusted certificate verifies the host but
carries the blast radius above.

For a Mac or other desktop browser the window also shows the
certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint (a new line, "Certificate", computed
from `identity.certificate`; Chrome and Safari on macOS show the same
value in their certificate viewer) as an optional comparison the owner can
make by hand. It is offered as optional and is not required for the page
to work.

The certificate stays as `make_identity` makes it
(`src/adapters/remote.rs:95`, no SubjectAltName). The spike records
whether Safari and Chrome offer "proceed" for it. If either does not, the
fix is an IP SAN added when the certificate is made at serve time. The
pin is the key, so reissuing the certificate invalidates no pairing.
`a_change_of_address_rebinds_the_port` (`tests/remote.rs:1494`) is where
that would be tested.

`authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127`) takes the token from `Authorization:
Bearer` and, absent that, from the cookie. Cookies are not isolated by
port, so another service on the same IP shares the jar, and the upgrade
request carries the cookie: both are request-forgery surfaces. So a
cookie-authenticated request that is not a `GET`, and every WebSocket
upgrade, must carry `Origin: https://<Host header>`. Otherwise it is
refused 403 `origin` before any command is translated. A bearer request
is never subject to this. Revocation needs no new path. The record is
gone, the cookie's hash is unknown, the next request is 401
`unauthorized`, and the socket closes as it does today.

*If the spike shows a browser refuses to store the `Secure` cookie from a
click-through origin, stop and take that to the owner before building on
it.* The fallback is a `localStorage` token and a single-use ticket for
the socket. That changes the threat model (decision 2 above), so it is not
built speculatively.
input.new_string:
`authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127`) takes the token from `Authorization:
Bearer` and, absent that, from the cookie. Cookies are not isolated by
port and `SameSite=Strict` does not separate ports of one IP (same site,
different origin), so a page served by another service on the same IP
sends the cookie with its requests, reads and upgrades included. A read
whose response a hostile page cannot read still leaks timing and, for a
subscription, holds a socket. So the rule covers **every
cookie-authenticated request, `GET` and upgrade included**; a bearer
request is never subject to it. Before any translation or reply, a
cookie-authenticated request is refused 403 `origin` unless all of these
hold:

1. `Host` is an IP literal, optionally with a port (never a name). A
   DNS-rebinding page reaches the host under an attacker's name, and a
   cookie bound to the IP is not sent there; this check also stops a
   request that arrives with a name in `Host`.
2. `Sec-Fetch-Site`, when the browser sends it, is `same-origin`
   (another port on the same IP is `same-site`, and is refused). The
   header is on Safari 16.4+, Chrome and Firefox.
3. `Origin`, when present, equals `https://<Host header>`. A WebSocket
   upgrade and every `POST` carry `Origin` in every browser, so for them
   it is required. A same-origin `GET` from `fetch` carries `Origin` in
   some browsers and not in others, so for a `GET` the rule is: `Origin`
   if present must match, and with no `Origin` the request needs
   `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`. A cookie `GET` with neither is refused,
   which also refuses a browser too old to send either; that browser
   cannot use the page, and the page says so ("this browser is too old").

Revocation needs no new path. The record is gone, the cookie's hash is
unknown, the next request is 401 `unauthorized`, and the socket closes as
it does today.

**This decision is conditional on the spike.** If the spike shows that
Safari on iPhone or Chrome refuses to store the `Secure` cookie from a
click-through origin, or does not send it on `fetch` or `wss://`, this
decision does not stand and the work stops before the cookie step (see
"Order"). The fallback is a `localStorage` token and a single-use ticket
for the socket, which puts the token within reach of any script on the
origin, changes the threat model, and so goes back to the owner as a new
plan rather than being built speculatively.

input.content:
# Response to feedback 1

Only `plan.md` in this directory was edited. The earlier plan is untouched.

1. **Trust step proves nothing.** Agreed, and the plan now says so. I took your options 2 and 4 together.
   - *Where it changed:* "Where this departs from the issue" (first bullet) and "Decision 1: the certificate".
   - The instruction to compare the key on the page is gone. The page's key is labelled "as the host reports it" and only tells two Switchboards apart.
   - Decision 1 now writes the weakening of §5 and design.md's "key verified before the code is sent" as a deliberate, scoped exception for a browser. It says what bounds it: the code's limits, the scope chosen in the window, the device showing in the dialog, and Revoke.
   - The plan marks the exception as needing owner sign-off, and the order has a step 0 that stops everything without it. I can't give that sign-off.
   - Option 1 (a real binding) is not available. A phone's certificate dialog shows neither the SPKI hash nor a usable fingerprint. The plan adds an optional "Certificate" SHA-256 line in the pairing window for desktop browsers, and says it isn't required.

2. **Dropping the JSON is a removal.** Agreed, and the plan no longer drops it.
   - *Where it changed:* "Decision 3: one URL", the UI section, the tests and "Contract additions".
   - "Copy invite" still copies the JSON, unchanged, with the `addresses` array. A new "Copy link" copies the URL, and `PairingInvite.parse` accepts both.
   - Only the QR payload becomes the URL. I searched `client/Sources` for a camera or scanner and found none, so no shipped client reads the QR.
   - The host's invite carries one address today, so nothing is lost.

3. **Reachability.** Fixed. I checked `bind_remote`: it binds loopback unless `identity.listen.lan` is set.
   - *Where it changed:* "The UI", new "Reachability" paragraph, with a test in "The tests".
   - On loopback the pairing window hides the QR and "Copy link" and tells the owner to allow the local network. With no network address it says that instead. The code, key and "Copy invite" stay.
   - A second UI test covers the loopback case, and the existing test now sets `listen.lan`.

4. **Origin rule incomplete.** Agreed, and the rule is wider now.
   - *Where it changed:* "Decision 2", the `authenticate` paragraph, and the Origin tests.
   - The rule now covers every cookie-authenticated request, reads and upgrades included. It needs an IP-literal `Host`, `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` when the browser sends it, and a matching `Origin` when present.
   - A cookie `GET` with neither header is refused. A browser too old to send either can't use the page, and the page says so.
   - Another port on the same IP is `same-site`, so it is refused.
   - I didn't make `Origin` mandatory on every `GET`. Same-origin `fetch` GETs omit it in some browsers, so `Sec-Fetch-Site` is the check there. `RemoteRequest` gains `sec_fetch_site`.

5. **One cookie for two hosts.** Fixed.
   - *Where it changed:* "Decision 2" and a new two-hosts test.
   - The cookie is `__Host-sb-<server_id>`, which `__Host-` allows, and `authenticate` reads only its own.
   - A collision can no longer produce the page's "revoked" state. A 401 means this host doesn't know the token.

6. **`/me` and fixtures.** Agreed. I said "no fixture" because only the page reads it, which was wrong.
   - *Where it changed:* "Port changes" (`/me`) and the tests' "Fixtures" bullet.
   - Added `client/Fixtures/me.json` from `write_fixtures`, a small `DeviceMe` type in Swift, and a line in `FixturesTests.swift`.

7. **Rate-limit accounting.** Specified now.
   - *Where it changed:* "Pools and rate".
   - `limited` first asks `web::is_page(path)`, the same fixed `match` that serves the files, and uses a separate `page` window.
   - Only page requests count. A WebSocket reconnect storm or API traffic can't lock out a reload, and a reload loop can't starve `/info` or `/pair`.
   - A page 429 is the JSON error with `no-store` and `nosniff`, and no CSP.

8. **JS untested; the spike can sink Decision 2.** I did not split the commit, because the task asks for one. The gate is now explicit instead.
   - *Where it changed:* "Spike first", "Order inside the one commit", "Decision 2" and "Contract additions".
   - The cookie and `wss://` rows must be measured on Safari on an iPhone and on Chrome before the cookie step starts.
   - If they fail, or there is no phone, the work stops with nothing committed and goes back to the owner.
   - The cookie items in the contract are marked conditional on the spike and the sign-off.
   - The tests section now says plainly what the Rust tests do and don't cover. I added a test that `replaceState` comes before the first `fetch` or `WebSocket` in `app.js`. The browser-only claims rest on the spike and the acceptance run.

9. **Process and docs.**
   - *Line 3573:* I checked it. It is the "Known gaps at the first merge" bullet inside the single "Remote client (2026-10-12)" section, which ends at `:3584`. The remote port has no "Milestone N status" block. The plan now says this and leaves that bullet alone. It adds a "The web surface" bullet before it and a "Known gaps of the web surface" bullet after it.
   - *Literal count:* it was a line count and was wrong. `grep -o` gives 28 literals in `src/app.rs` and 1 in the adapter (`:829`), 29 in all, plus any the compiler finds in `tests/` or the fakes.
   - *Embedding:* the plan now says `include_str!` in `src/adapters/web.rs`. `scripts/bundle.sh` copies binaries only, so it needs no change. `Cargo.toml` has no `include` list, and the Linux CI build needs nothing outside the crate.
   - *Spike in the same commit:* I kept it, as the task asks for one commit. The gate in point 8 is what keeps the order honest.

1	# Plan: a web control surface on the remote port (issue #230)
2	
3	Line references are to the worktree at `7fe8949` (branch
4	`dispatch/230-a-web-control-surface-the-remote-port-se`, clean).
5	
6	## Where this departs from the issue
7	
8	- **"The key in the URL lets a genuine page refuse to send the code to a
9	  host whose `/info` key differs."** The code does not bear out the
10	  strength of that. `/info` returns `spki_sha256` as a JSON string
11	  (`remote_info`, `src/app.rs:3568`) over the same TLS connection the
12	  page was loaded on, and a page script cannot see the connection's
13	  actual public key. A host that terminates TLS can serve a page and an
14	  `/info` that agree with each other. The comparison catches a stale or
15	  mistyped QR that points at a different Switchboard, and nothing else.
16	  The plan keeps the comparison for that, and nowhere calls it a check on
17	  the host. It also means a browser pairing **weakens the binding rule of
18	  `docs/remote-client.md` §5 and design.md's "Trust boundary", "pairing
19	  verifies the key before the code is sent"**: the browser sends the code
20	  (first in the `GET /?code=…`, then in `/pair`) to whatever answered the
21	  owner's click on the certificate warning, and the token comes back to
22	  that peer as a `Set-Cookie`. The plan writes that down as a deliberate,
23	  scoped amendment in §5 and design.md (decision 1) and **does not
24	  implement it until the owner signs it off**; the native paths keep the
25	  rule unchanged.
26	- **"The one-line excerpt the card shows."** The excerpt is not on the
27	  wire. It is built in the UI from the parsed conversation
28	  (`agent_excerpt`, `src/ui/cards.rs:558`, called at `:178`) or from a
29	  pane caption. `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:646` and the fields in
30	  `client/Fixtures/session.json`) carries `card`, the state label
31	  (`"starting"`, `"at a prompt (…)"`, `"exited (0)"`), plus
32	  `waiting_reason` and `notes`. Putting an excerpt in a listing means a
33	  transcript parse per session, which §4.1 keeps off the frame. The
34	  first cut shows the `card` label, and `waiting_reason` for a waiting
35	  session. The last response arrives on opening the session. An excerpt
36	  is a later, separate read-model item.
37	- **"A device's scope on the page."** The scope is only in the `/pair`
38	  reply, and a dialog change takes effect on the next request. After a
39	  reload the page cannot know it, and it cannot read its cookie. The
40	  plan adds `GET /api/v1/me`. The issue lists no endpoint, but the
41	  device's scope, "revoked" and "still paired" all need one.
42	- **"Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused."** True today
43	  (`strip_prefix("/api/v1/")`, `src/app.rs:3023`, and the 404 above it).
44	  The plan serves exactly three fixed paths outside it, before the
45	  frame is involved. It does not widen the prefix match.
46	- **"The `/pair` reply"** is `{token, scope, server_id, device_id}`
47	  (`src/app.rs:3656`). Decision 2 needs the token kept from script, so a
48	  browser asks for a cookie and its reply has no `token`. The native
49	  clients' request and reply are unchanged, so `pair.json` still decodes.
50	
51	## The record
52	
53	No change to any record. A browser is a `PairedDevice` (`src/ports/remote.rs:96`:
54	id, name, scope, `token_sha256`, created, `last_seen`) in `devices.json`,
55	saved through `RemoteFiles::save_devices` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:83`)
56	and found by `device_by_token` (`src/core/remote.rs:145`). Its name is
57	`device_name` from the page ("Safari on iPhone", from `navigator.userAgent`),
58	which `remote_pair` already takes (`src/app.rs:3650`) and defaults to
59	"Device". No `kind` field is added, so none of these versions moves:
60	`SCHEMA_VERSION` (16, `src/core/model.rs:12`), `VIEWS_SCHEMA_VERSION`
61	(7, `src/core/model.rs:612`) and `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` (1,
62	`src/ports/remote.rs:17`). `devices.json` has no version of its own, only
63	the array. Should an implementer find a device kind necessary after all,
64	the bump is the value in `model.rs` or `ports/remote.rs` at that time plus
65	one, with a step in `adapters::store::migrate`. Another ticket may have
66	taken the next number first.
67	
68	**Rehydration.** The host side is nothing new. The page keeps no state on
69	the host, `devices.json` survives a restart, and the same token hash is
70	accepted. `epoch` changes on restart and the page refetches (§4.4). The
71	device side is new, and has two parts:
72	
73	1. The token, in an `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` cookie that
74	   script never reads (decision 2).
75	2. A non-secret `localStorage` entry `{server_id, spki_sha256, name}`
76	   written at pairing, in a `try`. Without it the page cannot tell
77	   "never paired" from "revoked" or "identity changed", because it
78	   cannot read the cookie. A reload does this:
79	   - read the entry;
80	   - `GET /info`, and compare `server_id` and `spki_sha256`: a mismatch
81	     shows "identity changed, pair again" and sends nothing;
82	   - `GET /me`: 401 with an entry shows "revoked" and clears the entry,
83	     401 without one shows the unpaired screen.
84	
85	   With `localStorage` unavailable the page still works for the session
86	   and shows the unpaired screen after a reload that finds no cookie.
87	
88	The origin is `https://<ip>:<port>`, so cookie and entry belong to that
89	address. A Mac whose address changes is a new origin to the browser and
90	needs pairing again. The spec says so as a known gap, because a phone has
91	no Bonjour to follow the host.
92	
93	## The signals
94	
95	None new. The page is a fourth speaker of the existing protocol (§4.4):
96	it opens `wss://<host>/api/v1/events`, waits for `hello`, snapshots
97	`projects`, `projects/{id}/sessions` and `waiting`, applies buffered
98	events by revision, and refetches on `changed {session | sessions |
99	waiting | projects}`. A session that starts waiting changes the `waiting`
100	collection, so it moves to the top without a reload. For the open session
101	it sends `watch {conversation | screen}` when the view opens and
102	`unwatch` on leaving, and refetches on `changed`. On `resync_required` or
103	a new `epoch` it reloads everything, and it reconnects with back-off.
104	Redaction (§4.3) is applied before every cut on the host and is unchanged.
105	The page renders every host-supplied string with `textContent`, never
106	`innerHTML`, so a transcript cannot inject markup even if the CSP were
107	relaxed. The spec states that rule, and a test enforces it.
108	
109	## The actions and effects
110	
111	No `AppAction`, no `Effect`, no core state: serving a page and
112	authenticating a cookie are the port's job (`src/adapters/remote.rs`,
113	`serve_remote`), as `/info` is. Pairing, revoking and scope changes
114	already go through `Paired`, `RevokeDevice` and `SetDeviceScope`.
115	
116	**Decision 1: the certificate.** Click-through, not a downloadable
117	certificate. A downloaded certificate must be installed and then trusted
118	in full on the device (on iOS a profile, then Certificate Trust Settings).
119	That flow is heavy and easy to get wrong. It also trusts the certificate
120	for every name the device reaches, a wider grant than a per-address
121	exception. The click-through grants one browser an exception for one
122	address, which is all this surface needs. What it buys is encryption on
123	the wire and a browser that remembers the exception. What it does not buy
124	is any proof of whose certificate it is: on a hostile network an impostor
125	can present its own, relay the real host's `/info`, show the genuine key
126	digits, and the owner's click is what lets it. **So the page's key is not
127	a check and the plan does not tell the owner to compare it.** The page
128	still shows the host name and short key from `/info`, labelled "as the
129	host reports it", only to tell two Switchboards apart and to drive the
130	"identity changed" state. The browser's own certificate viewer shows the
131	certificate's fingerprint, not the SPKI hash, and a phone's shows neither
132	usefully, so no comparison is offered there either.
133	
134	The amendment, for the owner to sign off (this is the one open decision
135	the plan cannot make): **a browser pairs without the key having been
136	verified first. The only trust step is the owner's decision to open the
137	pairing window and scan its QR on a network they trust, with the code
138	single-use, five minutes and three wrong tries.** What bounds the damage:
139	the scope is chosen in the window (`read` by default), the new device
140	appears in the paired-devices dialog by name the moment it pairs, and
141	Revoke closes it. The window's text and the dialog say so in one
142	sentence: "A browser cannot verify this Mac's key. Pair a browser only on
143	a network you trust; check the device appears below, and revoke it if it
144	is not yours." §5 and the "Remote client" section of design.md gain that
145	sentence as a deliberate exception for the web page. If the owner declines
146	the amendment, the web page is not built, and the plan has no second
147	design to offer: a downloaded, trusted certificate verifies the host but
148	carries the blast radius above.
149	
150	For a Mac or other desktop browser the window also shows the
151	certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint (a new line, "Certificate", computed
152	from `identity.certificate`; Chrome and Safari on macOS show the same
153	value in their certificate viewer) as an optional comparison the owner can
154	make by hand. It is offered as optional and is not required for the page
155	to work.
156	
157	The certificate stays as `make_identity` makes it
158	(`src/adapters/remote.rs:95`, no SubjectAltName). The spike records
159	whether Safari and Chrome offer "proceed" for it. If either does not, the
160	fix is an IP SAN added when the certificate is made at serve time. The
161	pin is the key, so reissuing the certificate invalidates no pairing.
162	`a_change_of_address_rebinds_the_port` (`tests/remote.rs:1494`) is where
163	that would be tested.
164	
165	§5's rule is kept and amended: **before pairing, no bind serves anything
166	but `/info`, `/pair` and the page's own three files.** Every other path is
167	refused, loopback or not.
168	
169	**Decision 2: the token reaches the socket as a cookie.**
170	`POST /api/v1/pair` takes an extra body field `"session": "cookie"`. The
171	reply then omits `token` and sets
172	`Set-Cookie: __Host-sb-<server_id, 32 hex>=<token>; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=34560000`
173	(400 days, the cap browsers apply; the token does not expire and
174	revocation is the host's). **The name carries the host's `server_id`**
175	because cookies ignore ports: a second instance on the same IP
176	(`SWITCHBOARD_REMOTE_PORT`, or a second data directory) has its own
177	`server_id` and so its own cookie, and neither overwrites the other
178	(`__Host-` allows any name after the prefix). `authenticate` reads only
179	the cookie carrying its own `server_id`. A 401 therefore means this host
180	does not know the token, never that another host replaced it, so the
181	page's "revoked" state is not reachable by a collision. Two browsers' tabs
182	on different ports of one IP stay independent as well. A script never holds the token, `fetch` and
183	`new WebSocket` both carry the cookie, and the token is in no URL and no
184	`Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`. `localStorage` is readable by any script on the
185	origin and a cookie is not, which settles where the token lives. Native
186	clients send no `session` field and are unchanged.
187	
188	`authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127`) takes the token from `Authorization:
189	Bearer` and, absent that, from the cookie. Cookies are not isolated by
190	port and `SameSite=Strict` does not separate ports of one IP (same site,
191	different origin), so a page served by another service on the same IP
192	sends the cookie with its requests, reads and upgrades included. A read
193	whose response a hostile page cannot read still leaks timing and, for a
194	subscription, holds a socket. So the rule covers **every
195	cookie-authenticated request, `GET` and upgrade included**; a bearer
196	request is never subject to it. Before any translation or reply, a
197	cookie-authenticated request is refused 403 `origin` unless all of these
198	hold:
199	
200	1. `Host` is an IP literal, optionally with a port (never a name). A
201	   DNS-rebinding page reaches the host under an attacker's name, and a
202	   cookie bound to the IP is not sent there; this check also stops a
203	   request that arrives with a name in `Host`.
204	2. `Sec-Fetch-Site`, when the browser sends it, is `same-origin`
205	   (another port on the same IP is `same-site`, and is refused). The
206	   header is on Safari 16.4+, Chrome and Firefox.
207	3. `Origin`, when present, equals `https://<Host header>`. A WebSocket
208	   upgrade and every `POST` carry `Origin` in every browser, so for them
209	   it is required. A same-origin `GET` from `fetch` carries `Origin` in
210	   some browsers and not in others, so for a `GET` the rule is: `Origin`
211	   if present must match, and with no `Origin` the request needs
212	   `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`. A cookie `GET` with neither is refused,
213	   which also refuses a browser too old to send either; that browser
214	   cannot use the page, and the page says so ("this browser is too old").
215	
216	Revocation needs no new path. The record is gone, the cookie's hash is
217	unknown, the next request is 401 `unauthorized`, and the socket closes as
218	it does today.
219	
220	**This decision is conditional on the spike.** If the spike shows that
221	Safari on iPhone or Chrome refuses to store the `Secure` cookie from a
222	click-through origin, or does not send it on `fetch` or `wss://`, this
223	decision does not stand and the work stops before the cookie step (see
224	"Order"). The fallback is a `localStorage` token and a single-use ticket
225	for the socket, which puts the token within reach of any script on the
226	origin, changes the threat model, and so goes back to the owner as a new
227	plan rather than being built speculatively.
228	
229	**Port changes** (`src/adapters/remote.rs`, `src/app.rs`):
230	
231	- `RemoteRequest` (`:360`) gains `cookies: Vec<(String, String)>`,
232	  `origin`, `host` and `sec_fetch_site` (`Option<String>`), filled in
233	  `read_request` (`:444`) beside `bearer` (`:487`). `read_request` does
234	  not know the identity, so it keeps only the cookies whose names start
235	  `__Host-sb-` (at most four, each value capped at 64 bytes) and
236	  `authenticate` picks the one with its own `server_id`. None of them is
237	  logged. `RemoteReply` (`:389`) gains `headers: Vec<(String, String)>`,
238	  which `respond` (`:530`) writes after `Content-Type`. That means adding
239	  `headers: Vec::new()` to the `RemoteReply { … }` literals: counted with
240	  `grep -o`, 28 in `src/app.rs` and 1 in the adapter (`:829`), 29 in all,
241	  plus any the compiler finds in `tests/` or the fakes. A mechanical edit
242	  that `cargo build` completes.
243	- **Static paths are answered on the connection thread**, in `connection`
244	  (`:770`) before the request is handed to the frame, from a fixed `match`
245	  in a new `src/adapters/web.rs` (`pub fn asset(method, path) -> Asset`).
246	  The path is matched exactly and never joined to anything. They cost the
247	  frame nothing and do not use the 64-deep inbox. The set, `GET` only
248	  (anything else on these paths is 405 with `Allow: GET`; the query is
249	  ignored and never read):
250	
251	  | Path | `Content-Type` |
252	  |---|---|
253	  | `/` | `text/html; charset=utf-8` |
254	  | `/app.css` | `text/css; charset=utf-8` |
255	  | `/app.js` | `text/javascript; charset=utf-8` |
256	
257	  Anything else not under `/api/v1/` stays 404 `not_found` from
258	  `serve_remote`. Every static reply carries:
259	  - `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`.
260	    There is no `unsafe-inline` and no host. The HTML has no inline script
261	    or style, and carries `<link rel="icon" href="data:,">` so no favicon
262	    is requested. If the spike shows Safari does not match `'self'` to
263	    `wss:`, the explicit `wss://<Host>` source is added at serve time.
264	  - `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
265	  - `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`. **This is load-bearing:** the page's
266	    own URL holds the code, and without it the browser sends that URL as
267	    `Referer` with the request for `/app.js`.
268	  - `Cache-Control: no-store`, so nothing is cached across versions and no
269	    version is put in a URL.
270	  - `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`.
271	  - Never a `Set-Cookie`.
272	- **Pools and rate** (`:567-587`, `:631`). A static reply is
273	  `authenticated: false`, so a browser's connections sit in the pool of 4
274	  until its first authenticated call (the `events` upgrade or a read) moves
275	  them to the paired pool (`:835`). A browser may open up to six
276	  connections for a page. Past four, an accept is closed at once and the
277	  browser retries. The page is three files so keep-alive covers it with
278	  one or two. The pools are not changed: the spike counts the connections
279	  of a real page load, and only a measured failure changes the pool
280	  accounting. The only addition is `PAGE_PER_MINUTE = 60`: a `page`
281	  `RateWindow` beside `pair` and `info` in `Limits` (`:630`), and
282	  `limited` (`:631`) changes from an exact match on two constants to
283	  `if web::is_page(path) { &self.page }` before the existing arms, where
284	  `web::is_page` is the same fixed `match` that serves the files. One
285	  window is shared by the three paths. A load is three requests, so
286	  twenty loads a minute. Only page requests count: the events upgrade and
287	  every API call are not in this window, so a reconnect storm after a
288	  host restart cannot lock the owner out of reloading the page, and a
289	  reload loop cannot starve `/info` or `/pair`, which keep their own
290	  windows. A 429 on a page path is the same JSON error body `/info` gets,
291	  with `Cache-Control: no-store` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
292	  (so a browser never runs the body as script) and **no CSP**, which a
293	  JSON error that is not a document has no use for; `respond` takes the
294	  `headers` for it.
295	- **`GET /api/v1/me`** (`serve_remote`, after `authenticate`): `{device_id,
296	  name, scope}`, any paired device. The cheapest "am I still paired" probe
297	  and the one the revoke test polls. It goes in the §4.3 table, and its
298	  reply is a shared fixture: `client/Fixtures/me.json`, written by
299	  `write_fixtures` (`tests/remote.rs:1587`), decoded by a small
300	  `DeviceMe` `Decodable` in `SwitchboardProtocol` and a line in
301	  `FixturesTests.swift`. No native view calls it today; the fixture is so
302	  the wire shape is pinned on both sides like every other body.
303	- **Unpaired with no code and no cookie**, the page shows the host name
304	  and key (`/info`), "Not paired", and "Open Remote devices on the Mac,
305	  allow pairing, and scan its QR code", with `pairing_open` from `/info`.
306	  With a code and pairing closed (403 `pairing_closed`) it says so. On
307	  `wrong_key` it says "this is not the host whose code was scanned". On
308	  `wrong_code` it says the code was wrong or used.
309	
310	**Decision 3: one URL.** The pairing window's payload becomes
311	`https://<ip>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>` (the
312	address is IPv4, from `local_address`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:962`; the
313	alphabet needs no escaping). A pure
314	`core::remote::invite_url(address, server_id, spki, code)` builds it, so a
315	core test pins the shape. **The QR carries the URL, and nothing is
316	removed.** "Copy invite" keeps copying the JSON exactly as today
317	(`{server_id, spki_sha256, code, addresses}`), so every installed native
